speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned having occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after your tympanoplasty; could you tell me exactly when this pain started and what triggers it?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: The pain triggers you to have, and it seems related to eating and wearing earrings. Given your history of chronic ear infections and recent tympanoplasty, could you describe the nature of the pain—specifically, is it a sharp, electric sensation that radiates to your teeth or jaw, or does it feel like a deep ache inside the ear canal?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Ramsay Hunt Syndrome (Reactivation of Varicella Zoster Virus in the Ear).

The combination of shooting ear pain triggered by chewing (jaw involvement) and discomfort with earrings (sensitivity of the ear canal) following a recent tympanoplasty suggests reactivation of the virus affecting the geniculate ganglion and auriculotemporal nerve.

REQUEST IMAGES: Request for Otoscopic examination photos to look for vesicular rash in the external auditory canal or tympanic membrane.
